intro: Clergy counsel people, teach and lead communities, skills used in counseling, social work and education leadership. The closest of the 25 careers below is educational, guidance and career counseling, with an 88% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $64,330, which is 6% more than the $60,810 clergy earn.
why_it_works: Leading a congregation means preaching, comforting families in crisis, running programs and managing volunteers. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 4.12 out of 5 for clergy, and service orientation and instructing at 4. Counseling, social work and school leadership use the same strengths, and 19 of the 25 matches pay more. Every match needs no more education. The gaps are analysis and technology.
tips: Social and Community Service Managers earn $80,390, which is 32% more, and run programs like yours.
School administration pays $105,870, or 74% more, and values community leadership.
Counseling roles may need a state license; check requirements before applying.

faq.q: What jobs can former clergy do?
faq.a: The closest matches are educational, guidance and career counselors (88%), Social and Community Service Managers (83%) and child, family and school social workers (83%), based on O*NET 31.0. Healthcare Social Workers are 81% matched and earn $67,880, which is 12% more than the clergy median.

faq.q: Which careers for clergy pay more?
faq.a: 19 of the 25 matches pay more than $60,810. School administrators below the college level earn $105,870 (74% more), postsecondary education administrators $104,590 (72% more) and area, ethnic and cultural studies teachers $85,020 (40% more), according to BLS May 2025 data.

faq.q: Do clergy need another degree to change careers?
faq.a: Not more education in general: all 25 matches need no more than clergy already have. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 56% of workers in the closest match, though counseling and social work usually need a state license, which may require supervised hours.

The skills that most often need work are quality control analysis, operations analysis, systems analysis and programming. Judgment already rates 3.88 out of 5 for clergy in O*NET, so data and administrative skills are the main steps toward program and school leadership.
